content.user_title: Improve Ruby and Rails Code Quality
content.value_statement: Ruby projects often need clear idioms, tests, and performance checks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rails, gems, refactoring, and profiling.
actual_capabilities: Guides idiomatic Ruby refactoring with readable blocks, modules, mixins, and enumerables.
Applies Rails patterns for ActiveRecord models, controllers, views, and MVC structure.
Helps plan RSpec and Minitest coverage with fixtures, mocks, and clear expectations.
Supports gem development decisions, including dependency management and versioning.
Suggests performance profiling and benchmarking workflows with benchmark-ips.
Recommends RuboCop and static analysis practices for code quality.
limitations: It provides guidance and generated text, but it does not execute Ruby code by itself.
It cannot inspect private application behavior unless relevant files or requirements are provided.
It does not replace production testing, security review, or database migration checks.
It may need project-specific Rails versions and gem constraints for precise advice.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Ruby
use_cases.description: Modernize older Ruby methods with clearer structure, safer exceptions, and stronger tests.

use_cases.title: Review Rails Patterns
use_cases.description: Check model, controller, and view responsibilities against Rails conventions before a pull request.

use_cases.title: Prepare Gem Releases
use_cases.description: Plan gem structure, dependency boundaries, versioning, documentation, and release checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Ruby Method
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Ruby method for idioms and readability. Explain the changes before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Rails Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rails controller and model. Suggest clearer responsibilities, validation placement, and test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Test Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an RSpec or Minitest plan for this feature. Include fixtures, mocks, edge cases, and failure paths.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Ruby Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Ruby performance problem. Propose profiling steps, benchmark-ips cases, and safe refactoring options.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for help refactoring a long Ruby service method.
output_examples.output: A concise review with naming issues, enumerable suggestions, exception handling notes, and a focused test plan.

output_examples.input: A Rails team asks whether logic belongs in a controller, model, or service object.
output_examples.output: A responsibility breakdown with Rails convention guidance, tradeoffs, and recommended tests.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks how to prepare a Ruby gem release.
output_examples.output: A release checklist covering dependencies, versioning, documentation, tests, and quality tools.

best_practices: Share the Ruby, Rails, and gem versions before asking for architecture or dependency advice.
Provide failing tests, stack traces, or profiler output when asking for debugging or performance help.
Ask for both code changes and verification steps when the work affects production behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad rewrites without naming the desired behavior and constraints.
Do not accept metaprogramming suggestions without tests that document the generated behavior.
Do not treat generated optimization advice as complete without measuring it in the target application.

faq.question: Does this skill run Ruby code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and generated content for Ruby work, but it does not execute code by itself.

faq.question: Can it help with Rails applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on Rails models, controllers, views, ActiveRecord patterns, and MVC structure.

faq.question: Can it write tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan and draft RSpec or Minitest coverage when requirements and files are provided.

faq.question: Can it improve performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest profiling steps, benchmark-ips cases, and refactoring options for Ruby bottlenecks.

faq.question: Is it useful for gem development?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports dependency decisions, gem structure, versioning, and release preparation.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the relevant files, expected behavior, Ruby version, Rails version, and test output when available.
